nodes.label: The JSON escaping bug is the order of the two sed passes, not their presence
nodes.norm_label: the json escaping bug is the order of the two sed passes not their presence
nodes.summary: The existing bash collector escapes the double quote but not the backslash, so `grep -E \d+ f` produces invalid JSON and the parser drops the line. Both substitutions are present in both implementations; running the backslash pass first is what makes the quote pass safe, because the backslashes the quote pass introduces can no longer be doubled by a later pass. Measured both ways: the correct order round-trips, the reversed order raises JSONDecodeError at column 64.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-01 - fish-collector-and-docs-fix [ses_f0649ea65ffeR116fmTTLnvhHx].md:L04565] The bug is the order, not the presence of substitutions. Escaping the backslash first is what makes the quote pass safe, because the backslashes the quote pass introduces can no longer be doubled by a later pass. Chosen over python3 json.dumps at 18.7 ms per call against 0.7 ms for the sed pipeline, ~26x, on every interactive prompt.

nodes.label: Truncate before escaping, and count characters rather than bytes
nodes.norm_label: truncate before escaping with a character counting subcommand
nodes.summary: Two deliberate differences from the bash hook's `head -c 4000`, both stated as intent rather than silently inherited. `string sub -l 4000` counts characters, so a UTF-8 command is never cut mid-character where head -c can; and truncating before escaping means a long command can never be cut in the middle of an escape sequence, which would make the line unparseable. `string shorten` was rejected because it truncates to terminal display width and appends an ellipsis, corrupting the recorded command.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-01 - fish-collector-and-docs-fix [ses_f0649ea65ffeR116fmTTLnvhHx].md:L03786] string sub -l 4000 gives exactly 4000 whole characters with no ellipsis. Verified on fish 4.9.3: 5000 chars in, exactly 4000 out, and 4000 repetitions of a two-byte character survive whole.

nodes.label: set -l inside a fish if block is block-scoped and empty again at end
nodes.norm_label: set l inside a fish if block is block scoped and empty again at end
nodes.summary: A fish scoping rule that fails silently rather than loudly. Declaring the log path with `set -l` inside the TERMINAL_LOG_PATH branch scopes it to that branch, so it is empty again after `end`. The write is then handed an empty filename, which for this collector means flock is invoked as `flock -x ""`. The shipped code assigns first and overrides inside the block instead.

nodes.label: fish_preexec fires only interactively, so fish -c proves nothing
nodes.norm_label: fish preexec fires only interactively so fish c proves nothing
nodes.summary: status is-interactive returns 1 under `fish -c`, so neither event fires and a test that only ran fish -c would assert nothing at all while passing. The suite therefore calls the two handler functions by name, which is the same code path the event takes; end-to-end behaviour through a real pty is documented in a manual checklist instead, because a pty test is not deterministic. The same fact is written into the README troubleshooting section as a silent-failure warning.

nodes.label: Lock the log file itself rather than through a sibling lock file
nodes.norm_label: lock the log file itself rather than through a sibling lock file
nodes.summary: flock is given the log path itself, not a .lock sibling, so nothing extra appears in the user's log directory. The cost is that flock cannot create the file it locks, so the file must be touched first. Verified under ten concurrent writers times twenty-five lines: 250 lines, zero torn. util-linux flock rejects --no-fork together with -o, so the fork form is used deliberately.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-01 - fish-collector-and-docs-fix [ses_f0649ea65ffeR116fmTTLnvhHx].md:L07691] directly (flock -x $file cat >>$file) rather than through a sibling .lock file, so nothing extra appears in ~/.terminal_logs/. flock needs the file to exist, hence the touch.
